description:
P3 consumer-assertion: the '### Skill File-Tool Grants' subsection of plugin/governance/security-policy.md is the one canonical statement of which file-tool entries a skill's allowed-tools may carry, and CHECK 16 in tools/policy_check.sh is the guard that enforces it. The source pin holds the canonical heading, which CHECK 16 findings cite by name, so renaming or deleting the heading turns this fixture red. The set_check pins three literals in tools/policy_check.sh: the `=== CHECK 16:` section header (the block is present and still announces itself), `add_finding 'CHECK16'` (it still reports through the shared finding machinery, so --strict and the allowlist apply to it), and the `CHECK 16 DETECTION CANARY` section banner (the canary block has not been deleted). superset mode fails if any literal is removed; extras elsewhere in the file are ignored. Structural coverage this pin does not itself carry, but which exists inside tools/policy_check.sh: CHECK 16 is a positive allowlist over every discovered plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md. A Read, Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, Glob or Grep entry, bare or with parentheses, passes only as exactly the plugin cache Read rule built from the marketplace manifest's .name and its single ./plugin entry's name, or as `Edit(.hivemind/

)` with a non-empty

drawn from [A-Za-z0-9._*/-], no `..` segment and no leading `/`. Text from a whitespace-`#` onward is stripped before classifying. The six executor skills are exempt by path, and an exempt path that is missing or carries no bare file-tool entry is a stale-exemption finding. An unreadable or malformed manifest, no single ./plugin entry, or zero discovered skills is a finding. The detection canary runs the entry classifier on fixed strings in both directions. Residuals, stated plainly: this fixture claims only that these words exist in these two files. It does not pin the subsection's rule prose, so a rewrite of the allowed forms under an intact heading stays green here. A presence pin cannot prove the classifier still detects anything; that is what the in-check canary carries, and this fixture proves only that the canary section still exists, not that its assertions still run. It is blind to a narrowed file-tool list, a widened allowed form, a grown exemption list, or narrowed discovery, any of which leaves all pinned literals intact. CHECK 16 itself does not see a file tool reached under another name (an MCP tool or a future built-in), an allowed-tools key not at column 0, or the later lines of a multi-line YAML scalar entry.
